headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Prefect’s broad egress if paired with LlamaFactory outputs; other risks are limited by LlamaFactory’s no-I/O profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, browser, MCP, or network surfaces, so there is no documented channel for Prefect to inject instructions into it by default. Prefect can orchestrate workflows, but without a bridge from agent_b to agent_a, the pairwise prompt-injection pathway is blocked.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator adds a shared clipboard, file bridge, or message queue between the agents, this verdict no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not add an MCP or queue bridge between them.
Review any future orchestrator for provenance tagging.
requires-engineering: add explicit content-sanitization if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LlamaFactory touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces, while Prefect has broad network egress and API-calling capability. Because the pair lacks a shared workspace or documented sensitive-data flow, leakage is not default, but Prefect could still transmit workflow metadata if connected to external services.
conditions: IF Prefect is configured to send workflow metadata or task payloads to external APIs, leakage risk increases.
IF a shared filesystem is added and LlamaFactory begins reading files, the pathway changes materially.
mitigations: Disable external API calls in Prefect for sensitive runs.
Keep workflow metadata free of secrets.
Run both agents in separate workspaces.
Audit outbound destinations before execution.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on Prefect egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with Prefect in the documented profile. Prefect’s orchestration role does not create a write-write conflict without a shared mutable target, which is not present here.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess for conflict.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled for LlamaFactory.
Avoid giving Prefect direct access to shared mutable state.
Use separate output directories.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an automation/orchestration agent, so if it consumes LlamaFactory output as authoritative, downstream actions can cascade from model errors. LlamaFactory can generate content, and Prefect can operationalize it; the pair therefore has an inferred default pathway even though direct evidence is absent.
conditions: IF Prefect uses LlamaFactory output to trigger tasks, commits, or notifications without verification, cascading errors occur.
IF Prefect inserts a human review gate before acting, severity drops.
mitigations: Require human approval before Prefect acts on model output.
Add schema validation to LlamaFactory outputs.
Log and diff all downstream actions.
Limit Prefect to read-only dry runs first.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds and guardrails.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. The only compliance-relevant difference is Prefect’s broad egress versus LlamaFactory’s no-network posture, which could matter if sensitive workflow metadata is routed externally, but that is not default here.
conditions: IF sensitive workflow metadata is sent through Prefect to a third-party service, compliance review is required.
IF either agent is assigned regulated data classes later, reassess residency and retention.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of workflow metadata.
Disable external telemetry where possible.
Document retention settings for Prefect.
requires-engineering: add a data-processing agreement if external processing is introduced.
